articles.headline: Swansea's Labour council to widen popular NCN4 path between Dunvant and Gowerton
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has secured £500,000 from the Welsh Government Regional Transport Fund to upgrade a 1.75km stretch of NCN4 between Dunvant and Gowerton.
body: Swansea's Labour council is pressing ahead with more improvements to one of the city's best-loved walking and cycling routes, with a further section of National Cycle Network 4 (NCN4) set to be upgraded and widened.

The Labour-run council has secured £500,000 through the Welsh Government Regional Transport Fund to improve the section of NCN4 between Dunvant and Gowerton. The work will cover a 1.75km stretch, creating a wider, more comfortable and more accessible shared-use path for everyone who walks, wheels or cycles there.

This builds on the council's earlier widening and resurfacing work on NCN4 between Blackpill and Dunvant. Those improvements have been well received and have already helped improve access, safety and capacity on the popular Clyne Valley route.

NCN4 is one of Swansea's key active travel routes. It links communities including Gowerton, Dunvant, Killay and Blackpill, with onward connections towards Mumbles, Swansea city centre and neighbouring areas. The upgrade will give pedestrians, cyclists and people using mobility aids more room to pass each other, easing congestion and making the route better for commuters, families, leisure users and visitors alike.

Cllr Andrew Stevens, Swansea Council's Cabinet Member for Environment and Infrastructure, said: "This is another important investment in Swansea's active travel network and will build on the improvements already delivered between Blackpill and Dunvant."

He added: "By widening the path we can make it more comfortable, accessible and attractive for all users, giving people more space and helping to support safer journeys on foot, by bike and by other active travel means."

Some sections of the route will need to close temporarily while the work takes place, and users are asked to follow local signage and plan ahead during construction. Cllr Stevens said: "We appreciate that temporary closures will cause some disruption while the work is taking place, but these are needed to allow the improvements to be delivered safely. We will keep disruption to a minimum and make sure clear information is available for route users."
The Welsh Government's Regional Transport Fund supports transport investment across Wales, with a strong focus on walking, wheeling, cycling and public transport improvements.
This is Labour delivering step by step for Swansea: safer, greener and more accessible ways to get around, connecting our communities and making everyday journeys better for residents of all ages.
articles.sourceTitle: Popular Swansea walking and cycle route to be upgraded
